name: Pakistan Monument and Museum
assumptions: Petal tips 18 m above the deck for the outer pair (dossier single figure, element unspecified) and 16.8 m for the inner pair, fitted to head-on photos; small petals about 9 m, fitted to the same photos.
Deck 5 m above the arrival court, from a wall-against-person estimate in one dusk photo; the court is modelled as ground level.
Petal plan from OSM roofs with a centre fitted to the outer corners; the OSM tip positions carry satellite lean and were not used directly.
The three small petals sit in the gaps of the large ones, seen head-on; their radius is estimated.
Each petal is a smooth shell with an elliptical profile; the fit to the head-on photo silhouette is good but no drawings were found.
Back of the petals drawn as a stippled pale field with brick ribs, from one dusk photo and one low-resolution aerial; the front half of each outer petal is brick as in the head-on photos.
Mural reliefs and scroll vines are not carved: the mural fields are a stipple texture and the frame bands are drawn from the photos. Band layout is approximate.
Crescent wall radius, height 3.1 m and taper fitted to the head-on photos; panel count estimated.
Star pyramid 5.6 m high with five points and gold stars placed as in the close photo; star count approximate.
Deck depth, reflecting pool, bronze bowl, stair width and planted terrace tiers are estimated from photos.
Podium slot windows are slanted as in the east side photo; the count on each wall is derived from wall length (about 2.5 m spacing).
Viewing terrace position and radius from the OSM ring path; 24 arch positions with 2 left open at the steps, count estimated from photos.
Museum massing from OSM footprint, 7.5 m walls and stepped pale roof with a central skylight from aerial views; heights estimated. Museum facade windows not modelled.
The pillar height of 6.15 m comes from photo proportions against OSM's 2.4 m diameter; dossier value is the diameter only.
The suppress ring is the hull of the plaza and museum rings, so the OSM museum building is replaced by this model.
